title: Third moment bound for a coordinate derivative
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $F$ be a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$ of degree at most $k$, and let $i\in[n]$. Suppose the random variables $X_j:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are mutually independent, $0<\rho<1$, and each $X_j$ is $(2,3,\rho)$-hypercontractive. Suppose also that every $X_j$ has mean zero and second moment one. Then $\displaystyle\int_\Omega\left|X_i(\omega)\,D_iF(X(\omega))\right|^3\,d\mu(\omega)\leq (1/\rho)^{3k}\,\mathrm{Inf}_i[F_{\mathrm{cube}}]^{3/2}$, where $D_iF$ denotes the coefficient family formed from the Fourier coefficients of the Boolean-cube derivative of $F$, evaluated at $X(\omega)$, and $F_{\mathrm{cube}}$ is the Walsh-basis evaluation of $F$ on the Boolean cube.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$
The random variables $X_j$ are mutually independent under $\mu$
